summary: Once Australia's cheapest new electric car and now undercut by BYD's own Atto 1 and the Geely EX2, the Dolphin pairs a soft, comfortable ride with a surprisingly well-equipped, upscale-feeling cabin for the price, according to CarExpert, CarsGuide and WhichCar. Reviewers agree it is happiest as a city runabout: refined and efficient around town, but wind noise, mixed rear visibility and (on the base Essential) modest power blunt its appeal on the open road. It is not a driver's car, but on value and everyday livability it comfortably outpoints most petrol light hatches at a similar price.
pros: Essential undercuts the MG4 Urban Essence 54 and Atto 2 at $29,990 before on-roads while still offering 340km WLTP range
Comfortable, well-controlled ride for the segment
Roomy cabin and quality-feeling trim materials for the price
Strong standard equipment including a large rotating touchscreen
Five-star ANCAP safety rating with comprehensive driver assist tech
cons: Underpowered Essential struggles with highway overtaking
Slow 7kW AC home charging versus rivals' 11kW
Small boot and restricted rear visibility
Steeper resale depreciation risk as BYD repeatedly cuts prices, most recently a $28,888 drive-away Essential campaign for orders to 15 December 2026
